title: Asymmetric Beta Loss for Evidence-Based Safe Semi-Supervised Multi-Label Learning

problem.claim: Semi-supervised multi-label learning seeks to improve model performance by exploiting unlabeled data, but pseudo-labeling can perform poorly when unlabeled examples include out-of-distribution data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches commonly assume that labeled and unlabeled data share the same distribution, leaving a need for robust unlabeled-data exploitation under OOD contamination.

contributions.claim: A safe semi-supervised multi-label learning framework based on evidential deep learning is proposed for robust and effective exploitation of unlabeled data.
An asymmetric beta loss is proposed to improve robustness over common multi-label learning losses and address positive-negative imbalance in evidential deep learning losses for multi-label learning.

A dual-head structure generates class probabilities for pseudo-labeling and instance uncertainties for filtering OOD examples, together with a dual-measurement weighted loss that avoids threshold estimation during unlabeled training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets verify the method's effectiveness for OOD detection and semi-supervised multi-label learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets performance improvement in semi-supervised multi-label learning through unlabeled data.
Pseudo-labeling commonly assumes matched labeled and unlabeled distributions, but realistic collection processes can introduce OOD examples and degrade performance.
The authors propose an evidential deep learning-based safe semi-supervised framework.
The framework combines asymmetric beta loss, dual-head probability and uncertainty estimation, OOD filtering, and threshold-free weighted unlabeled training.
The authors report effectiveness on OOD detection and semi-supervised multi-label learning across multiple benchmark datasets.
